subject: Rate gateway penalty window causing customer production degradation
messages:
From: laura.chen@mediacorp.com
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Production errors & latency spikes — urgent

Rafael,

We started seeing elevated error rates and latency from the Redwood endpoint for our payments reconciliation flow around 14:50 PDT today. ~18% of calls are returning 429/503 and end-to-end latency has jumped from ~120ms to ~1.2s. This is impacting reconciliation and downstream billing jobs.

Attached is a screenshot from our dashboard with request error breakdown and a short wirelog from the failing calls. Please advise ASAP — our ops team is already receiving pager alerts.

Laura Chen
SRE, MediaCorp
Attachments: mediacorp_prod_metrics.png, wirelog-2026-06-24.txt
From: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
To: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.chen@mediacorp.com
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors & latency spikes — urgent

Stephanie / Grace,

Forwarding MediaCorp's report — they're seeing sustained 429/503s and latency spikes on the payments reconciliation route. Laura attached a wirelog and metric snapshot. Quick summary from our side (preliminary): we saw a regional burst spike at 14:40 PDT and the rate-gateway moved clients into a penalty window that aggressively curtailed burst credits for the tenant group. That guardrail looks like it didn't replenish correctly for long-running jobs.

Can infra/serving confirm whether the token-bucket replenishment task missed cycles for the us-west region? If so, we likely handed MediaCorp into a penalty state and their burst credits were exhausted, triggering broad rejections rather than graceful throttling. This is urgent — customer is paged.

If we need to escalate to execs for an SLA exception/credit, let me know after we confirm root cause.

- Rafael
Director, Customer Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.chen@mediacorp.com
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors & latency spikes — urgent

On Wed, Jun 24, 2026 at 3:45 PM Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Stephanie / Grace,
>
> Forwarding MediaCorp's report — they're seeing sustained 429/503s and latency spikes on the payments reconciliation route.

We've pulled logs from the rate-gateway and the serving runtime. Findings so far (high level):
- At 14:39:21 PDT we observed a traffic burst from MediaCorp that triggered the per-tenant burst accounting.
- The 'safety_penalty_window' for the tenant group was set to 120s but our replenishment window for burst credits had been inadvertently configured to 900s for the us-west pool during a recent deploy (INF-3478).
- The mismatch means the gateway applied a long blocking window while the serving runtime assumed a shorter window for admitting burst traffic. The result: rapid exhaustion of burst credits + repeated 429 responses across concurrent shards.
- We also saw request-level latency amplification because requests were rerouted across fallback model variants, adding model load and amplifying rejections.

Immediate actions we applied (16:05 PDT):
1) Reduced safety_penalty_window to 30s for the affected tenant group (manual override).
2) Pushed a hotfix to revert the replenishment-window to 120s for us-west (deployment INF-3492).
3) Enabled temporary increased burst cap for MediaCorp's tenant id to allow reconciliation jobs to drain (~+3x burst credits) while we stabilize.

MediaCorp — you should see error rate and latency improve within a few minutes; please confirm. We'll follow with a postmortem and plan to prevent this config drift.

-Stephanie
Sr. Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
Attachments: sla-impact-summary.pdf
From: laura.chen@mediacorp.com
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors & latency spikes — urgent

Thanks Rafael / Stephanie / Grace — latency and 200-rate have returned to normal for the reconciliation workflows and the job backlogs are draining. Error volume dropped to ~0.6% and median RTT back to ~140ms.

Two asks from our side before we close the loop:
1) A written timeline of events and the exact config changes you applied so we can reconcile with our incident timeline and Ops runbooks.
2) Requesting an executive-level note and a one-time credit for the customer impact window (billing window: 2026-06-24T14:40 to 2026-06-24T16:10). Our finance team expects documentation for the credit.

Laura Chen
SRE, MediaCorp
